text:
ConocoPhillips jumped 3.4% today, continuing a sharp two-week rally that's seen the stock climb 15.6%. The move reflects surging oil prices driven by geopolitical tension—Iran escalated attacks in the Strait of Hormuz this week, a critical shipping chokepoint, which pushed U.S. crude up sharply and created a wider gap between world oil prices ($126.55/barrel) and U.S. prices ($101.91/barrel). As a major oil producer, ConocoPhillips benefits directly when crude rallies, especially in a volatile environment where supply concerns dominate.

Beyond the immediate news, tanker rates have spiked so much that analysts are saying the "true" cost of delivered oil is roughly $30–$40 higher than the headline price suggests—a hidden cushion that insulates oil producers' profitability even if prices pull back modestly from current levels. This combination of geopolitical risk and tight physical supply is the engine behind the stock's recent surge.
